subject: Throughput ladder + smoothing proposal for POC MAP
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura@edgescale.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@edgescale.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Draft MAP & throughput targets for POC

Jonas —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. As promised, attached is our internal wish list for the POC and an initial MAP sketch. High level: we want to validate latency at 95th p95 < 350ms for customer-facing flows, and have a run of throughput tests that represent ~25M TPM peak.

For commercial planning we need a proposed monthly throughput ladder (tokens/month) so procurement can align budgets to months 1–12. Can you share a version that ties to milestones (POC completion, acceptance testing, ramp to pilot)?

Key constraints from our side: legal needs a clear rollback-credit if quality regressions happen at scale; procurement will only sign a 12-month agreement if we can smooth the first 6 months of token consumption.

Attaching our MAP outline for context. Happy to jump on a short call.

Best,
Laura
Senior Product Manager, EdgeScale
[Attachment: edgescale-map-outline.docx (DOCX, 72KB)]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura@edgescale.com>
Cc: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@edgescale.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft MAP & throughput targets for POC

Laura —

Thanks for the MAP. I pulled together a first pass that ties Redwood's evaluation milestones to a tiered throughput ladder and preliminary commercial terms (attached). Highlights:
- POC phase (month 0–1): up to 5M TPM, performance verification and latency SLO checks.
- Pilot phase (months 2–4): staged ramp to 15M TPM steady-state, with a canary at 8–10M TPM in month 2.
- Production ramp (months 5–12): smoothing to 40M TPM by month 8, with an option to accelerate to 60M TPM for an uplift discount.

I included suggested acceptance gates and rollback-credit language to address legal's ask. See MAP-draft-v2.pdf.

Quick Q: when Marissa and I model discounts, do you expect the production ramp to be treated as committed TPM for billing, or would procurement prefer a blended committed/overage approach? That affects the discount tiers we can offer.

Happy to chat today 2–4pm PT.

—Jonas
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: MAP-draft-v2.pdf (PDF, 120KB)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura@edgescale.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 08:40:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood counter: commits, ramp & discount table

Laura, Jonas —

Following our internal pricing review, here is a concrete counterproposal for commit volume and ramp smoothing we think balances risk for both sides:

Proposed commercial ladder (committed tokens/month):
- Months 1–2 (POC + Acceptance): 4M TPM committed (credit applied to overages).
- Months 3–5 (Pilot smoothing): 12M TPM committed.
- Months 6–12 (Production cadence): 36M TPM committed with a built-in pace schedule: +8M every two months starting month 6, up to 52M by month 12 if EdgeScale triggers the acceleration clause.

Discounts & credits:
- Baseline committed rate: standard hosted price.
- 7% volume discount at >=36M TPM committed.
- Additional 5% uplift discount if EdgeScale signs a 24/7 support add-on and commits to the acceleration clause.
- Quality rollback: if model-related regressions exceed the MAP-defined error budget for more than 48 hours, Redwood will issue credits equal to one week of committed TPS billing for the affected month.

Billing mechanics proposition: treat months 1–3 as blended (committed + true-ups) to give procurement smoothing while month 4+ transitions to committed billing with monthly true-ups. This keeps commitments conservative early while giving predictability later.

I attached the pricing grid (Redwood-pricing-counter-v1.xlsx) with examples and a sample cashflow for year 1. Let us know whether procurement prefers all committed billing (with a lower discount) or blended smoothing as above.

Cheers,
Marissa
Senior Sales Operations Manager, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood-pricing-counter-v1.xlsx (XLSX, 68KB)]

From: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@edgescale.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Chen <laura@edgescale.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood counter: commits, ramp & discount table

Marissa —

This is helpful — thanks. Procurement pushed back on the month 6 leap to 36M TPM; their ask is a gentler slope because our finance team needs to avoid big step-up budget approvals. Proposed smoothing from our side:
- Months 6–7: 20M TPM
- Months 8–9: 30M TPM
- Months 10–12: 40M TPM

We can still accept the acceleration clause but would prefer the trigger to be based on sustained usage >28M TPM for two consecutive months rather than an absolute date. The rollback-credit language looks good — can we get the exact SLO error budget wording for legal review?

Also procurement wants the first committed tranche to be no larger than 12M TPM so the initial PO stays under their approval threshold.

Happy to do a short call tomorrow to align on final MAP text and signature timeline.

—Marco
VP Product, EdgeScale

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura@edgescale.com>, Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@edgescale.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 14:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood counter: commits, ramp & discount table

Thanks Marco, Laura —

We can accept EdgeScale's smoothing request and update the MAP acceptance gates accordingly. Summary of agreed changes:
1) Months 1–3: blended commit, starting at 4M TPM (POC/acceptance) moving to 12M TPM by month 3.
2) Months 4–7: pilot ramp to 20M TPM (as requested).
3) Months 8–9: 30M TPM. Months 10–12: 40M TPM.
4) Acceleration trigger: sustained usage >28M TPM for two consecutive months to enable faster uplift and the associated discount.
5) Legal: we'll provide precise SLO/error-budget language (attached as a one-page addendum for review).
6) Procurement: initial PO limited to 12M TPM for months 1–3 to keep within approval thresholds; subsequent amendments can increase committed TPM per MAP schedule.

Next steps: I'll update the MAP and pricing spreadsheet to reflect smoothing and send a single doc for signature. Target dates: final MAP in HubSpot by 2026-11-27, DocuSign send by 2026-11-29, signed and countersigned by 2026-12-10.

If that timeline works, Marissa and Ben will start the amendment paperwork; Laura/Marco, let me know if you want a 30-minute alignment call tomorrow 10am PT.

Thanks —
Jonas
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: MAP-final-draft-edgescale.pdf (PDF, 85KB)]
